# Concurrent Linked Queue

A bare `LinkedList` is unsafe to share between producers and consumers because
its updates can race. This example compares a `LinkedList` whose `add()` and
`poll()` methods are synchronised with `ConcurrentLinkedQueue`, an unbounded,
thread-safe FIFO (first-in, first-out) queue. The bare list is not executed:
a failure would depend on scheduling and would be an unreliable demonstration.

Both implementations protect individual queue operations. The synchronised
wrapper uses mutual exclusion; `ConcurrentLinkedQueue` uses a non-blocking
algorithm without an application-level monitor. This example is not a benchmark
and does not establish which implementation is faster.

`poll()` returns `null` if the queue is empty; it does not wait for an element.
The queue has no fixed capacity and therefore supplies no capacity-based
backpressure. Use a suitable `BlockingQueue` when waiting for an item or bounded
capacity is required. An unbounded queue can grow until resources are exhausted.

## Learning objectives

By the end of this example, attendees can:

- distinguish thread-safe queue operations from a synchronised list wrapper;
- explain FIFO order and why sorted concurrent results do not demonstrate it;
- identify the queue’s happens-before guarantee for a transferred element; and
- describe empty-queue behaviour and the absence of capacity-based backpressure.

## Prerequisite

Install an
[Oracle Java 8](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java8) JDK
or newer and ensure `java` and `javac` resolve to it in your shell.

## The program to inspect

`LinkedListIntQueue` synchronises each operation on the same wrapper instance.
This provides mutual exclusion for access through that wrapper. An unlock also
happens-before a subsequent lock on the same monitor, providing visibility
between those operations.

```java
package demo;

import java.util.LinkedList;
import java.util.Queue;

import static demo.utils.Numbers.requirePositive;

public final class LinkedListIntQueue implements IntQueue {

    private final Queue<Integer> queue = new LinkedList<>();

    @Override
    public synchronized void add(final int number) {
        requirePositive(number);
        queue.add(number);
    }

    @Override
    public synchronized int poll() {
        final Integer value = queue.poll();
        return value == null ? NO_VALUE : value;
    }
}
```

`ConcurrentLinkedIntQueue` delegates to a `ConcurrentLinkedQueue`. Its
individual operations are thread-safe; a sequence of operations is not thereby
one atomic operation. The wrapper converts an empty `poll()` result from `null`
to `NO_VALUE` (`-1`); the underlying queue does not permit `null` elements.

The Java Memory Model (JMM) specifies visibility and ordering of shared state.
The queue’s API gives a specific happens-before guarantee: actions before a
thread places an object in the queue happen-before actions after another thread
accesses or removes that element. It does not cover later unsynchronised
mutations of the object. This example transfers integers rather than mutable
objects, so its output does not demonstrate publication of mutable state.

```java
package demo;

import java.util.Queue;
import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentLinkedQueue;

import static demo.utils.Numbers.requirePositive;

public final class ConcurrentLinkedIntQueue implements IntQueue {

    private final Queue<Integer> queue = new ConcurrentLinkedQueue<>();

    @Override
    public void add(final int number) {
        requirePositive(number);
        queue.add(number);
    }

    @Override
    public int poll() {
        final Integer value = queue.poll();
        return value == null ? NO_VALUE : value;
    }
}
```

`Main` first adds and removes an ordered range on one thread, showing FIFO for
that sequence. It then submits concurrent adds, waits for all of them to finish,
and submits concurrent polls. Producers and consumers therefore do not overlap
across those phases. The results are sorted to compare membership, so they do
not show removal order or establish FIFO under concurrent calls. Task and log
order depend on scheduling; neither timing nor a successful run proves the
queue’s memory-consistency guarantee. The executor is shut down in `finally`.

```java
package demo;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture;
import java.util.concurrent.ExecutorService;
import java.util.concurrent.Executors;
import java.util.stream.Collectors;
import java.util.stream.IntStream;

import static demo.utils.Logs.log;
import static demo.utils.Logs.logHeaderAndJavaVersion;

public final class Main {

    public static void main(final String[] args) {
        logHeaderAndJavaVersion("Concurrent Linked Queue");

        /* The number of items to be added to the queue, and then polled */
        final int range = 10;

        log("Check FIFO order using a synchronized LinkedList");
        final List<Integer> linkedListFifoOrder = loadUnloadInOrder(new LinkedListIntQueue(), range);

        log("Check FIFO order using a ConcurrentLinkedQueue");
        final List<Integer> concurrentLinkedQueueFifoOrder = loadUnloadInOrder(new ConcurrentLinkedIntQueue(), range);

        log("FIFO order:");
        log(" LinkedList + synchronized: " + linkedListFifoOrder);
        log(" ConcurrentLinkedQueue:     " + concurrentLinkedQueueFifoOrder);

        log("Load and unload numbers concurrently using a synchronized LinkedList");
        final List<Integer> unloadedLinkedList = loadUnloadUsingQueueThreadPerOperation(new LinkedListIntQueue(), range);

        log("Load and unload numbers concurrently using a ConcurrentLinkedQueue");
        final List<Integer> unloadedConcurrentLinkedQueue = loadUnloadUsingQueueThreadPerOperation(new ConcurrentLinkedIntQueue(), range);

        log("Concurrent results (sorted to compare membership):");
        log(" LinkedList + synchronized: " + unloadedLinkedList);
        log(" ConcurrentLinkedQueue:     " + unloadedConcurrentLinkedQueue);
    }

    private static List<Integer> loadUnloadInOrder(final IntQueue queue, final int range) {
        IntStream.range(0, range).forEach(queue::add);
        return IntStream.range(0, range)
                .map(ignored -> queue.poll())
                .boxed()
                .collect(Collectors.toList());
    }

    private static List<Integer> loadUnloadUsingQueueThreadPerOperation(final IntQueue queue, final int range) {
        /* The queue is loaded by the given number of values and then unloaded again using a thread per operation, thus,
            we need two times the given number of threads. */
        /* Only in Java 19 the ExecutorService implements AutoClosable! */
        final ExecutorService executor = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(range * 2);
        try {
            /* Load the values to the queue using a thread per value */
            final List<CompletableFuture<Void>> loaders = IntStream.range(0, range)
                    .mapToObj(number -> CompletableFuture.runAsync(() -> queue.add(number), executor))
                    .collect(Collectors.toList());

            /* Complete every add before polling. poll() does not wait for an item when the queue is empty. */
            CompletableFuture.allOf(loaders.toArray(new CompletableFuture<?>[0])).join();

            /* Unload the values from the queue using a thread per request/value. */
            final List<CompletableFuture<Integer>> unloaders = IntStream.range(0, range)
                    .mapToObj(number -> CompletableFuture.supplyAsync(queue::poll, executor))
                    .collect(Collectors.toList());

            /* Wait for all threads to complete */
            CompletableFuture.allOf(unloaders.toArray(new CompletableFuture<?>[0])).join();

            /* Return the unloaded values, which must be between 0 and the given range */
            return unloaders.stream()
                    .map(CompletableFuture::join)
                    .sorted()
                    .collect(Collectors.toList());
        } finally {
            executor.shutdown();
        }
    }
}
```

## Guided walkthrough

Run these commands from the `examples/concurrent-queue` directory. Choose one
of the following ways to run the example.

1. Run the example using the
   [Maven `exec` plugin](https://www.mojohaus.org/exec-maven-plugin/).

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean compile exec:exec
   ```
